gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically confirmed diagnosis of World Health Organization Grade IV glioma (glioblastoma or gliosarcoma)

candidate_evidence.quote: All patients will receive the study drug combination consisting of SurVaxM and pembrolizumab (PEM) with no randomization, stratification or dose escalation.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Study of Pembrolizumab Plus SurVaxM for Glioblastoma at First Recurrence

role_evidence.quote: The main purpose of this study is to assess the clinical activity of Pembrolizumab and SurVaxM in participants with recurrent glioblastoma.

arms: Arm A - Have not received immunotherapy
Arm B - Have failed prior anti-PD1 therapy

role_evidence.quote: [DRUG] SurVaxM (other names: SVN53-67, M57-KLH): 500 mcg per dose, dosed every two weeks for 4 doses and then every 3 months

arms: Arm A - Have not received immunotherapy
Arm B - Have failed prior anti-PD1 therapy

role_evidence.quote: [DRUG] Sargramostim (other names: GM-CSF): 100 mcg per dose, dosed every two weeks for 4 doses and then every 3 months

agents.drug_class_hint: recombinant GM-CSF; used here as vaccine adjuvant on the same schedule as SurVaxM

flag.reason: Licensed immunomodulatory protein given as a vaccine adjuvant on the SurVaxM schedule; could be treated as an investigational candidate (which would make pembrolizumab experimental_combination) rather than part of the excluded vaccine regimen.

arms: Arm A - Have not received immunotherapy
Arm B - Have failed prior anti-PD1 therapy

role_evidence.quote: [DRUG] Montanide ISA 51: 1 ml per dose dosed every two weeks for 4 doses and then every 3 months

agents.drug_class_hint: oil-based vaccine adjuvant (emulsifier), given with SurVaxM
arms: Arm A - Have not received immunotherapy
Arm B - Have failed prior anti-PD1 therapy

coder_notes: SurVaxM is a peptide cancer vaccine -> excluded_intervention_type; sargramostim (GM-CSF) and Montanide ISA 51 are given on the identical vaccine schedule and treated as components of the vaccine regimen (same regimen_id). Pembrolizumab is the only pharmacological investigational candidate. Sargramostim flagged because a licensed protein could alternatively be counted as a second candidate. Two non-randomised experimental arms defined by prior anti-PD-1 exposure; no control arm. 'WHO Grade IV glioma (glioblastoma or gliosarcoma)' without IDH requirement -> historical terminology.
